ontology.name: membrane
ontology.definition: A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

ontology.name: cGMP binding
ontology.definition: Binding to cGMP, the nucleotide cyclic GMP (guanosine 3',5'-cyclophosphate).

ontology.name: photoreceptor outer segment membrane
ontology.definition: The membrane surrounding the outer segment of a vertebrate photoreceptor.

ontology.name: intracellularly cAMP-activated cation channel activity
ontology.definition: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a cation by a channel that opens when intracellular cAMP has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

ontology.name: intracellularly cyclic nucleotide-activated monoatomic cation channel activity
ontology.definition: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a monoatomic cation by a channel that opens when intracellular cyclic nucleotide has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

ontology.name: intracellularly cGMP-activated cation channel activity
ontology.definition: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a cation by a channel that opens when intracellular cGMP has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

ontology.name: monoatomic ion channel activity
ontology.definition: Enables the facilitated diffusion of a monoatomic ion (by an energy-independent process) by passage through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel without evidence for a carrier-mediated mechanism. May be either selective (it enables passage of a specific ion only) or non-selective (it enables passage of two or more ions of same charge but different size).

ontology.name: plasma membrane
ontology.definition: The membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cell from its external environment. It consists of a phospholipid bilayer and associated proteins.

ontology.name: intracellular cyclic nucleotide activated cation channel complex
ontology.definition: A protein complex that forms a transmembrane channel through which cations ions may pass in response to an intracellular cyclic nucleotide binding to the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.

ontology.name: monoatomic ion transport
ontology.definition: The directed movement of a monoatomic ion into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Monatomic ions (also called simple ions) are ions consisting of exactly one atom.

ontology.name: monoatomic cation transport
ontology.definition: The directed movement of a monoatomic cation, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Monatomic cations (also called simple cations) are positively charged ions consisting of exactly one atom.

ontology.name: photoreceptor outer segment
ontology.definition: The outer segment of a vertebrate photoreceptor that contains a stack of membrane discs embedded with photoreceptor proteins.

ontology.name: monoatomic cation transmembrane transport
ontology.definition: The process in which a monoatomic cation is transported across a membrane. Monatomic cations (also called simple cations) are positively charged ions consisting of exactly one atom.

ontology.name: transmembrane transport
ontology.definition: The process in which a solute is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other.

ontology.name: cone photoreceptor disc membrane
ontology.definition: Stack of disc membranes located inside a cone photoreceptor outer segment, and containing densely packed molecules of opsin photoreceptor proteins that traverse the lipid bilayer. Cone disc membranes arise as evaginations of the ciliary membrane during the development of the cone outer segment and remain contiguous with the ciliary membrane.

ontology.name: transmembrane transporter complex
ontology.definition: A transmembrane protein complex which enables the transfer of a substance from one side of a membrane to the other.

ontology.name: signal transduction
ontology.definition: The cellular process in which a signal is conveyed to trigger a change in the activity or state of a cell. Signal transduction begins with reception of a signal (e.g. a ligand binding to a receptor or receptor activation by a stimulus such as light), or for signal transduction in the absence of ligand, signal-withdrawal or the activity of a constitutively active receptor. Signal transduction ends with regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. regulation of transcription or regulation of a metabolic process. Signal transduction covers signaling from receptors located on the surface of the cell and signaling via molecules located within the cell. For signaling between cells, signal transduction is restricted to events at and within the receiving cell.

ontology.name: visual perception
ontology.definition: The series of events required for an organism to receive a visual stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Visual stimuli are detected in the form of photons and are processed to form an image.

ontology.name: phototransduction
ontology.definition: The sequence of reactions within a cell required to convert absorbed photons into a molecular signal.

experimental_premises.interpretation: The mapped mouse Cngb3 donor has a same-term IDA from PMID:15634774. The actual Results report cone outer-segment CNGB3 as data not shown; this is positive ortholog localization, not direct human microscopy.

Human CNGB3 itself has same-term IDA from PMID:12815043. Wild-type CNGB3 changes cAMP responsiveness of CNGA3/CNGB3 channels; the target is a legitimate experimental descendant premise, with secondary physiological scope.

Human CNGB3 itself has same-term IDAs from PMID:12815043 and PMID:24164424. These human heteromeric-channel experiments provide legitimate target experimental grounding, not evidence of beta3-only current.

Human CNGB3 has same-term IDA from PMID:12815043, with enhanced surface localization on coexpression with CNGA3 and functional membrane currents. This supports the target premise independently of the ancestral placement.

The current IBD adds human CNGB3 among its seeds although it is absent from the original GOA WITH/FROM. Current same-term IMP from PMID:12815043 and independent human channel structures support complex membership; neither is substituted into the preserved original source fields.

Human CNGB3 has same-term IDA from PMID:37463923, where cGMP density occupies the beta-subunit pocket in the assembled channel. This supports target binding; it does not establish equivalent activity of the untested natural five-residue-deletion product.
